answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active association worker and 3 inactive workers. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 and discard 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards. Put the Animals Action card in the leftmost slot (strength 1); randomly place the other four Action cards in the remaining slots. All five start side I up. Starting appeal is staggered by turn order: first player 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.
answers.evidence: Personal setup: ‘Place one card side I up’; Animals under the leftmost slot; ‘Place your appeal...’ with first/second/third/fourth at 0/1/2/3; ‘Place 1 association worker... active’ and remaining 3; ‘Take 25 money’; ‘Draw 2 Final Scoring cards’; ‘Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4... discard the other 4.’

answers.answer: For a 2-player game, put 3 Base Conservation Project cards face up below the board and block the left level on the left card, middle level on the middle card, and right level on the right card; also block the three spaces in the donation area's left column. For 3 players, put 3 base projects face up and there are no stated blocked spaces. For 4 players, put 4 face up and there are no stated blocked spaces. Reveal the initial 6-card display after every player has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup says ‘In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up... otherwise the 3 topmost’; the 2-player-only clause lists the blocked levels and donation spaces. Personal setup G says, ‘After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.’

answers.answer: After using the card in slot 4, remove it; shift the cards that were left of that empty slot (slots 1–3) one slot to the right, then put the used card in slot 1. Set strength before performing the action. Each X-token spent adds +1 strength and returns to supply; any number may be spent, but you can hold at most 5 X-tokens. An ‘after finishing’ effect occurs after the action is complete, including Action-card movement.
answers.evidence: Turn procedure: ‘remove the card from its slot, shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right, and place the used card in slot 1.’ X-token strength is set ‘before performing the action’; max 5 held. ‘After finishing’ waits until the action, including moving the cards, is complete.

answers.answer: No. You may not take a regular action that plays zero animals or builds zero buildings. Instead, use the alternative X-token action: select an Action card, take exactly 1 X-token, move that card to slot 1, and shift intervening cards right. Its slot strength and upgrade state do not matter. You cannot take this action if you already hold 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: ‘You may not do nothing’; use the alternative X-token action. The X-token action says ‘take exactly 1 X-token,’ still move the selected Action card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards, and it is unavailable at 5 X-tokens.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional movement and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. The break happens after that player's current turn ends, so they finish the turn. After the break, play continues clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track: ‘the break takes place after the end of your current turn,’ you get ‘1 X-token,’ and ‘Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space.’ Break procedure: play continues clockwise with the next player.

answers.answer: Both Cards sides advance the Break token 2 spaces. On side I, choose either a deck draw according to the strength table (up to 3 cards, with the indicated discard), or snap exactly 1 display card at strength 5 or more; snapping has no deck draw. On side II, draw from the deck and/or from the display within reputation range, in any order, using the upgraded table; alternatively snap exactly 1 display card at strength 3 or more. The reputation restriction applies to side-II draws, not snapping. Display cards taken are replenished only after the turn is complete. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard down to the hand limit during breaks.
answers.evidence: Cards action: each side advances the Break token 2 spaces; side I draws or snaps at 5+, side II draws from deck and/or within reputation range or snaps at 3+. ‘On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation’; display is not replenished until turn completion. ‘You only discard to your limit during breaks.’

answers.answer: ‘Within reputation range’ means the display card in the folder matching your reputation plus all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action (Cards II); upgrading it allows progress past 9. Above 15, the marker remains at 15 and each further reputation step gives 1 appeal. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation range is ‘the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders.’ Reputation 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15, ‘1 appeal per remaining reputation step’; discard pile may not be inspected.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than strength. Build II may build any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in the same action. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building along an edge. Build only on empty spaces, cannot extend off-map or cover water/rock, and restricted-icon spaces require Build II. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately grants +1 appeal once.
answers.evidence: Build I: ‘exactly 1 building’ and ‘2 money per space’; Build II: ‘as many different buildings as you like’ within total strength, never 2 identical. Placement rules specify border for the first building, adjacency thereafter, unavailable terrain/restricted spaces, kiosk spacing, and pavilion appeal.

answers.answer: Build I allows standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo (size 3). Build II additionally allows a Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary, each size 5. The supply has four tiles of each special enclosure type; each zoo may have only one of each type. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: Building table lists the available types, sizes, and minimum Build side; ‘four tiles of each special enclosure’ and one of each type per zoo. ‘Unique buildings can never be built with this action’ and full-map coverage grants 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that same action. Resolve items one at a time and pay for each item before receiving its own benefits. Placement bonuses are taken immediately before the next building; ‘after finishing’ bonuses wait until the entire action is complete, including card movement. For simultaneous effects, the player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn structure says bonuses gained earlier ‘may be used for later steps of that action’ and ‘You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits.’ Build II says take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold ‘after finishing’ bonuses until the whole action ends. The summary says the owning player chooses the order of simultaneous effects.

answers.answer: For each animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its cost, house it legally, place its card, and resolve its effects. A partner zoo from the animal's continent reduces its cost by 3 money per continent icon on the card; a double icon therefore gives two such reductions. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the required size; after admission flip the whole enclosure to its occupied side, and it normally houses one animal. A Petting Zoo animal must go in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles and some birds may use their special enclosure, occupying the number of spaces shown with player tokens; special enclosures are not flipped. Water/rock requirements count distinct adjacent hexes and also apply when using a special enclosure. Ordinary effects resolve immediately, including before the next animal; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the Animals action is complete. Simultaneous effects may be ordered by the player.
answers.evidence: Animals action enumerates conditions, payment, enclosure, card placement and effects. The partner discount is ‘3 money per continent icon’; standard enclosures require at least the size and are flipped; special enclosure spaces are marked with tokens. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes; after-finishing effects wait until the entire action.

answers.answer: Animals II allows playing animals from the display within reputation range, with an additional cost equal to the folder number. Animals may be a mix of hand and display cards, and the display is not replenished until the turn ends. At strength 5 or more, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, raising the range before choosing display animals. Animals whose conditions show the upgrade-required icon are also allowed.
answers.evidence: Animals II: play from display within reputation range ‘paying an additional cost equal to the folder number’; at strength 5+ increase reputation ‘at the very beginning’; display replenished only after turn; may play animals with the upgrade-required condition.

answers.answer: Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, and only once per new building, you may move all suitable animals that fit from standard enclosures; choose separately for each animal. Mark the animal's indicated number of special-enclosure spaces with supply player tokens. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements (including terrain) back to empty. If none meets all requirements, use the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size requirement, flip none. The special enclosure is never flipped.
answers.evidence: Build II allows moving ‘all suitable animals that fit’ immediately and only once per building. Animal housing marks the number of spaces with tokens and never flips special enclosures. The edge-case section specifies the smallest qualifying standard enclosure, then fallback to size alone, then none.

answers.answer: The four Association task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, and conservation project work 5. Association I performs exactly one task. Association II may perform one or more different tasks whose total value does not exceed strength. Each task requires worker(s): normally 1, but if one of your workers is already on that task you must place 2; if 3 are there, you cannot repeat it until after the break. Other players' workers do not matter.
answers.evidence: The task list gives strengths 2/3/4/5. Side I is ‘exactly one’ task; repeat rules require two workers when one is already there and prohibit it with three. Side II allows different tasks up to total strength. ‘Other players' workers on a task do not matter.’

answers.answer: Partner zoos and universities are taken from available tiles on the Association board and placed on the lowest available space in the corresponding column of your map; take any printed space bonus immediately. You cannot take a partner zoo from a continent you already have, and may have at most 4; the third or fourth requires Association II. You cannot take duplicate universities. Board stock is replenished at each break so each tile is available once, skipping tiles all players already have. Universities grant any printed reputation when acquired; they are the only way to raise the hand limit to 5 (otherwise it is 3). A university tile can provide two research icons, one research icon plus 2 reputation, or hand limit 5 plus 1 reputation.
answers.evidence: Association task descriptions specify board-to-map placement, immediate bonuses, different continents, max 4, Association II for third/fourth, no duplicate universities, and university hand limit. The FAQ says bonus tiles take an available Association-board tile; break procedure replenishes each once.

answers.answer: Association I conservation work can support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately. Association II can also play a new project from the display within reputation range, paying its folder number. To support a project, fulfill an unoccupied condition and place one player token from the left edge of your map on it; each project may be supported only once by you. Take the conservation/reputation award and uncover that token's map bonus immediately, choosing whether the token bonus comes before or after the project reward. If a new project exceeds the player-count limit above the board, discard the rightmost card and return its tokens to their owners' supply—not to their map; their map bonuses remain activated. Limits are 2/3/4 face-up projects for 2/3/4 players; base projects remain below the board and are never moved.
answers.evidence: Association work specifies hand-play and immediate support, unoccupied conditions, one support per project, map token and immediate bonus timing. Side II allows display play with folder cost. The overflow rule returns tokens to supply and states base projects never move.

answers.answer: A release project's printed standard-enclosure size must match the animal's required standard size exactly, whether or not it could also live in a special enclosure. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, before gaining conservation; discard it and lose its icons. Retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. If it could live in a special enclosure, remove its indicated special-enclosure tokens if possible; otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, otherwise the smallest occupied enclosure meeting size alone, otherwise none if no occupied enclosure meets the size. A new Release into the Wild project gives 1 reputation; later support of one already in play does not.
answers.evidence: Release rules say the standard size must match ‘exactly’; lose only printed appeal before conservation, discard the animal and lose icons, while keeping conservation, reputation, ability appeal and earlier effects. The specified special-token and enclosure-flip fallback follows.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand if strength is at least its level and its conditions are met. Alternatively, advance the Break token by the action's strength and take that much money, even if fewer spaces remain before the break. Sponsors II plays one or more cards from hand and/or the display within reputation range; the sum of levels must be at most strength + 1, and display cards cost their folder number extra. Resolve cards one at a time, completing each card's instant effects before the next; after-finishing effects wait until the action finishes. Do not refill the display until the turn ends. The side-II break-money option gives twice the strength in money.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I states exactly one hand card or break advancement for strength and full strength money even if the track needs fewer steps. Sponsors II sums levels against strength +1, allows display cards with folder cost, resolves each before the next, and pays money twice for the break option.

answers.answer: Break steps are: (1) discard to hand limit, normally 3 or 5 with the particular university; (2) return Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; (3) recall all association workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; (4) discard display folders 1 and 2, slide the others down, and refill; (5) take income: appeal-based money, kiosk income, then break income on Sponsors and activated map bonuses; (6) reset the Break token. Each kiosk earns 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count, but empty special enclosures do. If several players take display cards during income, refill after each player. Where an order is needed, begin with the break initiator (or the affected player closest to them) and proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: The numbered Break procedure gives the order, hand limit, qualifying kiosk neighbors, and income order. It states to refill after each player taking display cards and gives clockwise ordering when effects require it.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus token next to that space. The first player to reach or pass 10 makes all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, each player discards one before scoring. Check the end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits for your own turn end or a break to trigger it, unless another player triggers the end first. After an end triggered at a player's turn end, every other player gets one final turn; if triggered during a break, every player gets one final turn. A Final Scoring card can give no more than 4 conservation points. Victory points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area of your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player with the most conservation-project supports, then tied players share the victory.
answers.evidence: Conservation track gives the rewards at 2, 5, 8 and 10. End conditions are checked at own-turn end or during a break, with distinct last-turn rules. Final scoring caps a single Final Scoring card at 4 conservation; VP formula and project-support tiebreak are stated.
